exec.heading: Execution
exec.toolParallelHint: Run multiple tools in one turn; off runs them one by one.
exec.generalToolsHint: How many file reads, foreground terminals, and searches can run together in one turn. Background terminals are separate.
exec.subAgentHint: Max concurrent sub-agents in this session (foreground and background). Background terminals count too.
exec.mediaToolsHint: How many image, video, and media-understanding jobs can run together in one turn.
exec.thisRoundHint: Max consecutive tool calls in this turn.
exec.subTaskHint: Max consecutive tool calls inside each subtask. Subtasks are for small scopes; max 500.
exec.concurrentTasksHint: How many independent tasks can run at once. Chat, schedules, and webhooks share this; the same session still queues.
exec.contentLimitsHint: Caps for uploads, file reads, search, and terminal output returned to the AI. Video uploads still use separate compression. Tool args can only lower these.
exec.uploadHint: Max size for chat uploads, excluding video.
exec.bodyHint: Max body size returned from a single file read.
exec.lineHint: Max bytes kept per line when reading or searching.
exec.grepHint: Max results returned from one search.
exec.terminalHint: Max terminal output per stream returned to the AI; excess keeps the tail.
exec.terminalTimeoutHint: Idle timeout is the default when unset; commands may override. Max wall time is a hard cap; tool args can only lower it.
exec.idleHint: Used when a command omits timeout. Ends the command if there’s no new output; output resets the timer. 1–86400 sec.
exec.maxWallHint: Max wall-clock time from start to forced stop, 1–10000 hours.
